data.claim: The 541 knobs across 50 sections render as TOML literals that parse back equal, independent of host and hash seed, in about 16 KB; the 16 default gates add about 8.5 KB when fields equal to GateDef defaults are left out. data.body:
NOTE 2026-10-18 (RH-contradictions-2026-10-18, contradiction #3): D-written-defaults-are-marked (accepted 2026-10-18) settles this: each value init/adopt/upgrade writes into .ddflow/conf.d carries a managed marker (origin packaged@<version>) and a digest. D-upgrade-config-changes treats an UNEDITED marked value as ddflow's (an upgrade may move it and shows it in the plan); an edited value or one without a marker is the operator's and is never changed without confirmation. Acceptance: init writes the marker; an upgrade moves an unedited marked default; an edited one triggers confirmation.

ORIGINAL TEXT (before RH-contradictions-2026-10-18):
ddflow ships ddflow/templates/default.toml holding every default value and the default workflow (gates, pipelines, flow). First stage: GENERATED from the section declarations (`ddflow config defaults --write`) and pinned by a recipe so it can never drift (pin recipe + test); second stage (CE-defaults-source) makes it the source of values. Loader reads it as the lowest layer. `ddflow config defaults` prints it. Measure its load cost. CONFORMANCE: governed by D-config-engine and research R-config-engine-2026-10 (read both first); every knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt (r-everything-configurable); reuse shared engines, no second layering mechanism (B-org-layers is the layer stack); files under 20 KB; upgrade-manifest fragment per knob; no new MCP tool (the tools/list budget has almost no headroom: extend ddflow_configure); the hook path must not get slower: add a measured import/load budget to the acceptance test.

SCOPE NOTE 2026-11-05 (sw-cedefaults): the managed-marker acceptance in the NOTE above is not met here and is left to CE-topic-split and CE-upgrade, which carry the identical NOTE: D-written-defaults-are-marked governs values written into .ddflow/conf.d, and nothing loads conf.d until CE-confd-loader, which depends on this item. [gate.*] tables are generated and pinned but load_gates reads them only from CE-defaults-source. No ddflow_configure parameter yet: DX-configure-defaults-param. Size: 25 KB, over the 20 KB in the CONFORMANCE boilerplate and under D-small-files-30k's 30 KB, which the test pins.

CE-defaults-file gave the CLI ddflow config defaults; over MCP only the knob rows of ddflow_configure reach the same values. Add a defaults parameter once B-main-red-core-tools-budget is green and surfaces/tools is free: tools/list is over its ratchet. The file is 25 KB, above the 20 KB result ceiling, so it needs the cut-and-say handling of mcp_bound. Writing stays on ddflow_view pins regenerate.

chunk_findings.detail: The `write` guard only checks that `D.PACKAGED_DEFAULTS` resolves under `repo`, which does not guarantee the running `ddflow` is the source-tree copy. If `ddflow` is installed in a virtual environment inside the repository—for example `/repo/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/ddflow/templates/default.toml`—then `path.resolve().is_relative_to(Path(repo).resolve())` is true, so the guard passes and `D.write()` overwrites the installed package’s template file instead of regenerating the source-tree file (or being refused, as the docstring requires for an installed `ddflow`). The check needs to ensure the `ddflow` code being executed comes from the repo, not just the template path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup/config.py:_packaged_defaults

chunk_findings.detail: A damaged `ddflow/templates/default.toml` that places a dunder key under a real section — for example `[core] __class__ = "broken"` — is not skipped as an unknown knob. At line 61 the guard is `not hasattr(target, knob)`, and every Python object already has attributes such as `__class__`, `__module__`, `__dict__`, and (for dataclass instances) `__dataclass_fields__`. So `hasattr(target, knob)` returns `True`, the value comparison fails, and `_apply_knob` is called for a key that is not a config knob. This contradicts the docstring’s promise that unknown knobs are skipped without a word, and depending on how `_apply_knob` handles the name it either emits a misleading warning or raises an uncaught exception instead of warning once and leaving the built-in defaults in place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_packaged.py:61

chunk_findings.detail: When `--write` is combined with `--set` (for example, `ddflow config --set some.key value --write`, or `ddflow config --set defaults --write`), `_names_defaults` routes to `_config_defaults` because `a.write` is true, but `_config_defaults` rejects the command solely because `a.set` is true and prints `--write goes with `defaults`: ddflow config defaults --write`. The message is wrong for that input: the failure is not that `--write` is missing `defaults`—the user did supply `defaults` as the value—but that `--set` cannot be used with the defaults subcommand. This sends the user toward `ddflow config defaults --write`, which is the intended form, without explaining why their actual command was rejected.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/setup.py:279

chunk_findings.detail: `test_write_regenerates_inside_the_tree` monkey-patches `DT.PACKAGED_DEFAULTS` to a temp file, then calls `API.configure(..., defaults=True, write=True)`. The API surface is implemented in `ddflow/api/setup/config.py`, which the manifest says adds `_packaged_defaults`; it therefore almost certainly writes to `_packaged.PACKAGED_DEFAULTS`, not to `DT.PACKAGED_DEFAULTS`. Because `DT` and `_packaged` are separate modules, `monkeypatch.setattr(DT, "PACKAGED_DEFAULTS", target)` leaves `_packaged.PACKAGED_DEFAULTS` pointing at the real shipped file. The result is that `API.configure` either regenerates the real `ddflow/templates/default.toml` (a working-tree mutation) or refuses the write because the real path is not under the temp `tmp_path`, so `out.exit` is not 0 and `target` still contains `"stale\n"`. The test should patch `_packaged.PACKAGED_DEFAULTS` (e.g. via the existing `packaged` fixture) so the API and the loader agree on the target.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_default_toml.py:220

chunk_findings.detail: A syntactically valid but stale `templates/default.toml` is applied, not passed over. For example, if a knob’s current Python default is `10` but the shipped file still contains `5`, `getattr(target, knob) == raw` is `False`, `_apply_knob` accepts `5`, and the effective Config uses `5` with no warning. This contradicts the stated contract that a damaged, missing, or wrong file warns and leaves built-in defaults, and it lets a forgotten `pins regenerate` silently change effective defaults.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_packaged.py:apply_packaged

chunk_findings.detail: `_config_defaults` only validates `a.set` and `a.value`; it does not reject other `config` flags such as `--filter`, `--append-toml`, `--local`, or `--explain`. For example, `ddflow config defaults --append-toml 'foo=1'` is routed here by `_names_defaults` (because `value == ["defaults"]`), but `_config_defaults` calls `A.configure(... defaults=True, write=False)` without passing `append_toml` and still returns `OK`. The requested TOML append is silently dropped while the command reports success; it should either apply the flag or print an error for the unsupported combination.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/setup.py:_config_defaults

chunk_findings.detail: `current()` calls `PACKAGED_DEFAULTS.read_text("utf-8")` with no error handling. If `ddflow/templates/default.toml` exists but is damaged (for example, contains invalid UTF-8 bytes like `\xff`), `.is_file()` is true and `read_text` raises `UnicodeDecodeError`. The exception propagates through `write()` and `main()`: `python -m ddflow.views.default_toml --check` crashes with a traceback instead of reporting the file as stale and returning 1, and `ddflow config defaults --write` cannot overwrite the damaged file to repair it. This violates the stated behavior that a damaged file warns and leaves built-in defaults so pin regeneration can still run, and it blocks the recovery path exactly when the file is damaged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/default_toml.py:current

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds CE-defaults-file stage 1 work but includes no `.ddflow/tasks/*.toml` record naming its phase, `needs`, and `wave:N`, which violates [r-task-phase-needs-wave]. The manifest lists every changed file in the review and contains only code, test, and pin files, so this task is missing the required task metadata.

chunk_findings.detail: The stray-flag validation uses truthiness, so an explicitly passed falsy value escapes detection. Given `ddflow config defaults --write --append-toml ''`, `a.append_toml` is `''`, `if given` is false, so `stray` is empty and the command proceeds to `A.configure(c.repo, A.ConfigEdit(defaults=True, write=True), ...)`, rewriting the packaged `default.toml`. The command should instead return `FAIL` and not write, because the command’s own contract printed here is “`config defaults` takes only --write” and `--append-toml` was supplied.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/setup.py:_config_defaults

chunk_findings.detail: This test asserts a wall-clock best-of-five `apply_packaged(Config())` is under `LOAD_BUDGET_MS = 25.0` ms. On a shared CI runner with cold page cache, CPU throttling, or a slow filesystem, a single first read/parse/comparison can exceed 25 ms even though the implementation is correct, so the test will fail nondeterministically. The performance budget depends on the executing host, not on behavior, and re-running only five times still does not make it deterministic.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_default_toml.py:test_the_load_cost_stays_inside_its_budget
ddflow/config/_packaged.py:53

chunk_findings.detail: A known section whose packaged value is not a table is dropped with no warning. Given `default.toml` containing `review = "not-a-table"` (and `review` in `cfg._sections()`), line 69 treats that the same as an unknown section and `continue`s, so `Config.load` keeps the dataclass defaults and never calls `_say`. That breaks the contract that a value no knob can take warns and is passed over; the file looks healthy, so the operator is not pointed at `ddflow pins regenerate`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_packaged.py:69

chunk_findings.detail: The stage contract says a value no knob takes must warn and leave built-in defaults. This test writes `[lease] no_such_knob = 1` and `[no_such_section] x = 1`, then requires `Config.load(None, env={}).unknown_knobs` empty and `capsys.readouterr().err == ""`. That input therefore locks in a silent drop, so a packaged file that names a removed or mistyped knob never surfaces drift and never points at `pins regenerate`.

chunk_findings.detail: When `write` is false, the function calls `path.read_text("utf-8")` without first checking that the file exists or catching `OSError`/`UnicodeDecodeError`. `ddflow config defaults` on a missing `ddflow/templates/default.toml` raises `FileNotFoundError`, and on a file containing invalid UTF-8 (for example `b"\xff"`) raises `UnicodeDecodeError`. The `if not text` branch that is supposed to report the file as missing is unreachable for an actually missing file, and both inputs violate the stated contract that an unreadable file warns and leaves built-in defaults instead of crashing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/setup/config.py:_packaged_defaults

chunk_findings.detail: The change removes the `PACKAGED_DEFAULTS.is_file()` guard and calls `read_bytes()` unconditionally. If the packaged defaults path is a non-regular file—for example, a FIFO created at `ddflow/templates/default.toml` with `mkfifo`—`Path.read_bytes()` blocks waiting for a writer and never returns, so `ddflow config defaults --check` hangs instead of warning or returning stale. The new `except OSError` cannot help because opening/reading a FIFO blocks rather than raising `OSError`. The previous `is_file()` check would have returned `""` for a non-regular file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/views/default_toml.py:current

chunk_findings.detail: The test is titled “changes nothing,” but it only reads and compares `repo/.ddflow/config.toml`. A regression where `config --write` (or `config --set lease.ttl_s 9 --write`) regenerates or overwrites the repository’s packaged defaults file before returning exit 1 would still pass, because that file is never read or asserted. The side effect this test exists to prevent is not actually checked.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_default_toml.py:test_write_without_defaults_changes_nothing

chunk_findings.detail: The stage contract says a value no knob takes must warn and leave built-in defaults. This test writes `[lease] no_such_knob = 1` and `[no_such_section] x = 1`, then requires `Config.load(None, env={}).unknown_knobs` empty and `capsys.readouterr().err == ""`. That input therefore locks in a silent drop, so a packaged file that names a removed or mistyped knob never surfaces drift and never points at `pins regenerate`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_default_toml.py:test_a_key_the_code_lost_is_skipped_silently

chunk_findings.detail: The drift check compares the dataclass default to the parsed TOML value with Python equality before `_apply_knob` can validate the raw value. That hides a bad value when it is equal under Python equality but invalid for the declared type. For example, a field declared `enabled: bool = False` and a packaged line `enabled = 0`: `read_toml` returns an `int` `0`, and `getattr(target, "enabled") != raw` is `False != 0`, which is `False`, so `_apply_knob` is never called and no bad-value warning is emitted. TOML booleans are only `true`/`false`, so an integer `0` is a bad value for a bool knob; the contract says a bad value must warn and leave the built-in default, but this path leaves it silently.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_packaged.py:_lay_section

chunk_findings.detail: The test requires the shipped pinned `default.toml` to load with `capsys.readouterr().err == ""`, even though its own docstring says the file contains `[gate.*]`, “no section of `Config`.” That is a key the declarations lack, so per the change’s contract it must warn as drift and point at `pins regenerate`. The valid TOML spelling `[gate."*"]` yields a `gate` table absent from `Config`; if the shipped file contains it, this test forces `_packaged` to keep a silent-drift exception of exactly the kind the change just rejected for `[no_such_section]`, and the test will fail if the product follows the contract by warning.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_default_toml.py:test_the_shipped_file_loads_without_a_word

chunk_findings.detail: Given packaged `default.toml` containing only keys the declarations lack (`lease.no_such_knob`, `[no_such_section]`), `apply_packaged` warns via `_say_drift` and never includes `_BUILT_IN`. The new test requires `pins regenerate` on stderr, so that input fails the test and does not tell the operator to regenerate the pin, unlike the bad-value and non-table warnings.
